The operator \(\vec{P}\) represents the spin angular momentum of a muon, a spin-1/2 particle. Its components are given in terms of the Pauli matrices:  
\(P_x = \frac{\hbar}{2} \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\),  
\(P_y = \frac{\hbar}{2} \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix}\),  
\(P_z = \frac{\hbar}{2} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}\).  
For a direction \(\vec{n}\) in the \(x\)-\(z\) plane, we can write \(\vec{n} = (\sin\theta, 0, \cos\theta)\) where \(\theta\) is the angle from the \(z\)-axis. The spin operator along \(\vec{n}\) is  
\(\vec{P}\cdot\vec{n} = \frac{\hbar}{2} (\sin\theta\,\sigma_x + \cos\theta\,\sigma_z) = \frac{\hbar}{2} \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta & \sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & -\cos\theta \end{pmatrix}\).  
The eigenvalue equation \(\vec{P}\cdot\vec{n}\,\chi = \frac{\hbar}{2}\chi\) reduces to \((\sigma\cdot\vec{n})\chi = \chi\), i.e., the eigenvector of \(\sigma\cdot\vec{n}\) with eigenvalue \(+1\). The standard normalized spinor for spin up along a direction with polar angle \(\theta\) and azimuthal angle \(\phi=0\) is  
\(\chi = \begin{pmatrix} \cos(\theta/2) \\ \sin(\theta/2) \end{pmatrix}\).  
This matches option (B). The other options include factors of \(\hbar\) or incorrect trigonometric functions.

Answer: B

Finally, the $Z-$component, $P_z$ of the operator is given by the product of $\hbar/2$  and another 2 by 2 square matrix having elements in the first row as $(1, 0)$, and that in the second row as $(0, -1)$.
